name: Andai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: only a sociolinguistic survey (Kassell/MacKenzie/Potter 2017, SIL, access 403) and Haberland 1966 classification; nothing that would describe stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid anda1283 Andai (record + references page)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 0 grammar/phonology/sketch references; Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Kassell et al. 2017, Haberland 1966, Haberland 1963, all a wordlist or less. Dialects Andambit, Imboin, Kaiyam, Kupin, Namata; ELP link labels the language 'Meakambut'.

sources.citation: Heeschen, Volker & Darja Hoenigman. 2026. Songs in Eipo, Yale, Awiakay and Meakambut, four Papuan languages. In Riesberg, Reinoehl & Hellwig (eds.), The Documentarist Turn (SLCS 240), 314-342. Benjamins (OA). doi:10.1075/slcs.240.13hee
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Song-language chapter; Meakambut (allied with Andai) described sociolinguistically (64 speakers, semi-nomadic); no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia: 'Andai language' and 'Arafundi languages' (revisions of Jan 2026)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tertiary; only villages, classification and Usher's proto-forms; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Arafundi River; Andai. New Guinea World (UZH DokuWiki, last modified 2024; Google Sites version via the Internet Archive 2020-10-16 and 2022-10-06).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative/historical only: Proto-Arafundi segment inventory and correspondence tables with Andai (Kayam, from Kassell) forms; source inventory for Andai = Haberland 1966:62-64 (Imbwain), Dye n.d. (Avambro), Kassell et al. 2017 (Imboin, Kaiyam). Andai subpage is empty in every version. Nothing on stress or prosody.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison, Bonnie MacKenzie & Margaret Potter. 2017. Three Arafundi Languages: A Sociolinguistic Profile of Andai, Nanubae, and Tapei. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2017-003. Dallas: SIL International. 60 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.3.2.2 'Stress', p. 17 (PDF p. 22): 'Stress was only marked on Wambrumas list, and even there, MacKenzie did not indicate stress on every word. As a result, only tentative conclusions about stress can be drawn. It appears that stress was generally on the ultimate syllable..' Wambrumas = Nanubae (nanu1240), Table 5 p. 14. Nothing about Andai stress; the two Andai wordlists (Imboin-Namata, Kaiyam; Appendix D pp. 48-54) carry no stress marks (0 x U+02C8/U+02CC in the text layer). Sec. 2.3.2.1 gives joint phone charts (Tables 6-7) for all three varieties.

sources.citation: Hoenigman, Darja. 2015. 'The talk goes many ways': registers of language and modes of performance in Kanjimei, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU. hdl 1885/155259.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Awiakay (awia1234), not Andai. Fig. 1.4 / p. 46 places Anday, Namata, Kaiyam (and Meakambut) in 'Upper Arafundi'. Appendix A Awiakay phonology: only a remark that each diphthong 'carries a single stress' while a vowel sequence carries primary + secondary stress (text-layer ll. 14942-14957). Nothing on Andai stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik Languages: Checklist and Preliminary Classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entries 137 Alfendio (Arafundi) and 138 Meakambut, pp. 39-40.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Village lists, test-wordlist codes (DCL71), pointer to Haberland 1966 wordlists; notes Meakambut 'closely related' to Alfendio but a separate language on his data. No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Hoenigman, Darja. 2025. Awiakay (Arafundi). In Nicholas Evans & Sebastian Fedden (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Papuan Languages. Oxford: Oxford University Press. 47 pp.

sources.note: Sister language (awia1234), not Andai, but the only first-hand stress statement in the family (abstract: 'primary stress occurs on the first syllable'); needed to judge any family-level expectation for Andai and to check whether Hoenigman comments on Upper Arafundi/Meakambut prosody from her own Meakambut fieldwork.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432 (Arafundi section pp. 232-238). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
